html:
Oracle bone writing is the oldest known form of written Chinese, carved on bones and turtle shells by the diviners of the Shang kings from about 1250 BCE.

The bones were used to ask questions of the royal ancestors. A diviner drilled hollows in an ox shoulder blade or a turtle shell, applied heat until it cracked, and read the answer in the cracks. Then the question, and sometimes the result, was carved next to the cracks: will it rain, will the harvest be good, will the king's attack succeed, will the queen's childbirth go well.

About 150,000 inscribed pieces are known, almost all from Yinxu, the last Shang capital near Anyang. The earliest come from the reign of King Wu Ding, radiocarbon dated to about 1254 to 1197 BCE. The last nine Shang kings are all named.

Their modern discovery is a good story. In 1899 a scholar named Wang Yirong is said to have noticed old writing on "dragon bones" sold as medicine. The trail led to Anyang, and scientific digging there began in 1928.

Why they matter:

  • They proved that the Shang, known from later histories, were real, and gave the names of their kings.
  • The script is already a full writing system, so writing in China is probably older still.
  • It is the direct ancestor of Chinese characters, used without a break to this day.

After the Zhou conquest, divination by bones became rarer and writing moved to bronze vessels and bamboo strips.
sum: Oracle bone writing is the oldest known form of written Chinese, carved on bones and turtle shells by the diviners of the Shang kings from about 1250 BCE.
